title: The brew caveat sends a machine to bootstrap only when the old keg is gone, so a deferred cleanup breaks the gate later
body:
Found by ic on 2026-09-23 while re-reading the 3.2.1 CHANGELOG entries. The caveat was added by 0527 (landed, in 3.2.1).

**What happens.** The formula's caveat, written by `bin/.devbin/cmd/macos` (lines 1611 to 1622), tells a machine upgrading from 3.2.0 or earlier to run `intent bootstrap` if the pointer file "names an Intent under Cellar/intent/ that is no longer installed". Homebrew can leave the previous keg on disk after `brew upgrade`, when cleanup is deferred or switched off. The old keg then IS still installed, the reader concludes the caveat does not apply, and the pointer keeps naming a versioned keg. The next `brew cleanup` removes that keg, and every commit in a project with the gate installed is refused, which is 0527's original failure, arriving later and away from the upgrade that caused it.

**What the fix has to do.** The caveat covers every pointer that names a versioned keg under `Cellar/intent/`, whether or not that keg is still on disk, and names `intent bootstrap --check` (0533), which reports a versioned-keg pointer, as the way to tell. It is a `bin/.devbin` edit, so the macOS bats are owed with it.

**Fixed** on vc's routing (2026-09-23). The caveat now sends a machine to `intent bootstrap` whenever its pointer names a keg under Cellar/intent/, whether or not that version is still installed, and says that `intent bootstrap --check` (0533) shows where the pointer sends the gate. The macOS bats arm asserts the new phrases and refuses the old one.

**Landed** at 5411b6bd6, patch-id 56aa13ee2f4b on the blob and on the landed commit, judged in dc's tail run, which vc passed. It reaches a machine only through the formula the 3.2.1 cut publishes.
